answer: Identity verification begins with physical memory commitment: an agent allocates 64 GB of volatile DRAM filled via a deterministically seeded cipher stream. The verifier probes this space with pseudo-random pointer chases, splitting queries like a prism across non-contiguous physical addresses. Responses must return within an 82-nanosecond budget to ensure reads hit local bus hardware rather than pooled network storage. A single cache-miss delay exceeding 120 nanoseconds fails the check, ejecting the node before the epoch summit and burning its registration stake.
